classification.difficultyReason: Decompose each right triangle into three triangles whose perpendicular heights are the common incircle radius, then solve for that radius.

children.label: a
children.prompt: $ABC$ is a right-angled triangle with a right angle at $B$. The circle shown is the ‘incircle’ of the triangle. Find the radius, $r$, of the incircle.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC with sides 4, 3 and 5, a dashed red incircle, three perpendicular radii to its points of tangency, and right-angle marks at B and all three tangencies. Ordinary source-blue lines become house black.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,0), B=(4,0), C=(4,3). Incircle centre (3,1), radius 1; tangencies (3,0), (4,1), and (2.4,1.8). These construction coordinates are not printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied side lengths, vertex labels, radius symbol r and perpendicularity marks are visible; no numerical radius is printed.

answer.short:
$1$

Join the incircle’s centre to the vertices and equate the sum of the three triangle areas to the area of $ABC$.
answer.worked:
Join the incircle’s centre to $A$, $B$ and $C$. The three resulting triangles have bases $4$, $3$ and $5$, each with perpendicular height $r$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{ABC}&=\frac12\times4\times3\\A_{ABC}&=6\\A_{ABC}&=\frac12(4r)+\frac12(3r)+\frac12(5r)\\A_{ABC}&=6r\end{align*}$$
Thus $6r=6$, so $r=1$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the radius of the incircle of a right-angled triangle with sides $5$, $12$ and $13$.

answer.short:
$2$

Use the common incircle radius as the perpendicular height of three triangles with bases $5$, $12$ and $13$.
answer.worked:
The hypotenuse is $13$, so the perpendicular sides are $5$ and $12$. Join the incircle’s centre to the three vertices. Each resulting triangle has perpendicular height $r$ to its corresponding side.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times5\times12\\A&=30\\A&=\frac12(5r)+\frac12(12r)+\frac12(13r)\\A&=15r\end{align*}$$
Thus $15r=30$, so $r=2$.
